touches.text: Inference Ticket: the record of one call to the inference proxy, everything that happened to that request.
Used for learning, or for debugging when something fails. A logging artifact, so disposable after 30 days.
INTENTION:
Knowledge: one list of nodes, owned by the librarian.

The librarian owns every tree and delegates ownership of some to the devices that learn: CodeMother, chart, any learning block holds its own trees by the librarian's delegation (Law 6: delegation through the owner's gate). Why: two holders with different weights over the same nodes have different perspectives and can debate points, and the librarian, asked anything, can look at the query from both. (Akien 2026-11-05)

Delegation nests down the rungs: the librarian delegates a set of trees to a device, the device to its machines, a machine to its tools if one is ever that complex. Each stays co-owned by the one above. CodeMother's learning goes in its own tables, and she owns the learning blocks of her machines and tools. (Akien 2026-11-05)

The memory model. Everything Cairn keeps as LEARNING in database memory is these five things, and only these. It does not say all information lives in trees: logs, troubles, git records and a device's own state keep their own homes (4.3.2-4.3.4). One kind of access everywhere. (Akien 2026-11-05)
Trees as tables, permanent: each asks one question, with the weights in its leaves.
Transient: the transient tree (what the logging tree becomes).
Each kind of thing declares its lifetime, and it ages out on that clock.

Cairn owns all of ~/.cairn/ and delegates each ~/.cairn/devices/ subtree to its device. Everything outside devices/ (~/.cairn/logging/ and the rest) is Cairn's, so every log is Cairn's and Cairn cleans them up in sleep. Transient things are files there. Trouble tickets are logging items.
Owns the graph trees: the one list of nodes, and each depositor's index over them (4.3.1.2).
Is the embeddings device's biggest user (16): its embeddings are tree histograms from there, not vectors from the inference proxy's embed verb. (Q#9, Akien 2026-11-03)
INFERENCE PROXY DEVICE (cairn/devices/inferenceproxy/; was inference_domain)
Every call makes an inference ticket (3.3.2): trees first, then the cheapest route the nest finds.
A request seen before is answered from the stored answer, if it still holds, and the host is not touched. That untouched call is compilation.

The stored answers are learning, so they live in the memory model (4.3.1.8): a tree the proxy holds by the librarian's delegation (4.3.1.6), asking "what did this request answer?". The meter (every call, its verdict and cost) is not learning: it is the inference ticket, a file in the logs tree on the 30 day clock (4.3.2). (Akien 2026-11-05)

NOT HOW IT IS NOW (measured 2026-11-05): one table, inference_calls, does both jobs: 11,395 miss rows carry the stored answers, 9,416 hit and 58 refused rows are meter only. The logs tree already holds the same calls as tickets (11,942 files). The librarian copies answers into its nodes separately (librarian/ingest.py, 250 so far), so the answers are kept twice.
EMBEDDINGS DEVICE (cairn/devices/embeddings/)

tree: the nexus graph-tree face (deposit, counsel, propose) over the librarian's trees. It is the same tool everywhere, not chart's: it is written as chart's only because chart was where it was first defined at that level. It stays a tool and does not fold into the librarian's verbs; a learning block holding its trees by the librarian's delegation (4.3.1.6) works them through it. A learning block that needs a special adaptation gets a subclass. (Q#54, Akien 2026-11-05)
